key_insight: UR-VC shows that normalized demo time is a noisy stand-in for real robot progress, and it learns to automatically correct these time-derived labels without requiring human annotations. This makes dense progress signals more accurate for robot learning, especially in contact-rich manipulation tasks.
problem_solved: Robot learning often needs dense progress or value labels to guide policies and detect task completion, but true step-by-step supervision is expensive and rarely available. The paper addresses the noise and mismatch in using normalized demonstration time as a proxy for physical task progress.
method: Start from time-derived progress labels from demonstrations as weak supervision.
Learn an unsupervised correction mechanism that adjusts these labels to better match true task progress.
Use the corrected value signals to improve intermediate-state evaluation, policy learning, and completion detection.
impact: For practitioners, UR-VC offers a scalable way to turn cheap demonstration timestamps into more reliable training signals. This can improve robustness and performance in robotic manipulation without adding manual labeling overhead.
